title: Prescribed quotient filtrations in a finite tower of exact functors
statement:
Let $t\in\mathbf N$, let $\mathcal A_a$ for $0\leq a\leq t$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and for $a<t$ let $T_a:\mathcal A_{a+1}\to\mathcal A_a$ be additive exact functors [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor; def-galois-exact-functor]. Let $H_a\in\mathcal A_a$ with $H_t$ a zero object. For every $a<t$ let $K_a\in\mathcal A_a$ and let
$$0\longrightarrow K_a\xrightarrow{u_a}H_a\xrightarrow{\pi_a}T_aH_{a+1}\longrightarrow0$$
be short exact, meaning that $u_a$ is a kernel of $\pi_a$ and $\pi_a$ is a cokernel of $u_a$. Fix for each $a<t$ a finite increasing filtration by subobjects $0=K_{a,0}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_{a,n_a}=K_a$; a subobject is a monomorphism modulo isomorphism, and the quotient $Q_{a,s}=K_{a,s}/K_{a,s-1}$ is the cokernel of its inclusion. Inclusions need not be strict. For $a\leq c$ write $T_{a,c}=T_a\circ\cdots\circ T_{c-1}:\mathcal A_c\to\mathcal A_a$, with $T_{a,a}$ the identity.

For every $a\leq t$, $H_a$ admits a finite filtration of length $\sum_{c=a}^{t-1}n_c$ whose successive quotients are isomorphic to $T_{a,c}Q_{c,s}$, ordered first by $c\geq a$ and then by $1\leq s\leq n_c$. At stage $a$ the filtration may be chosen as the images $u_a(K_{a,r})$ followed by the inverse images $\pi_a^{-1}(T_aL_s)$, where $L_\bullet$ is the chosen filtration of $H_{a+1}$; $\pi_a^{-1}(0)=u_a(K_a)$ and
$$\pi_a^{-1}(T_aL_s)/\pi_a^{-1}(T_aL_{s-1})\simeq T_a(L_s/L_{s-1}).$$
Inverse image means the pullback of a subobject along $\pi_a$. No splitting of any displayed short exact sequence is assumed. The assertion includes $t=0$ and all $n_a=0$, with the empty filtration of a zero object. If isomorphism-invariant classes $P_{a,v}\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal A_a)$ indexed by $v\in\mathbf R$ satisfy $T_a(P_{a+1,v})\subseteq P_{a,v}$, and $Q_{a,s}\in P_{a,v_{a,s}}$, then the resulting quotient indexed by $(c,s)$ belongs to $P_{a,v_{c,s}}$. Thus the assigned labels and every common real upper bound of them are retained.

proof.text: Put $N_a=\sum_{c=a}^{t-1}n_c$. We construct the asserted filtration for every $a$ by descending induction, retaining its ordered quotient isomorphisms. At $a=t$, $N_t=0$ and the zero object $H_t$ has the empty filtration. For the induction step fix a filtration $0=L_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq L_m=H_{a+1}$ supplied at $a+1$, where $m=N_{a+1}$. Write $H=H_a$, $K=K_a$, $u=u_a$, $\pi=\pi_a$, $B=T_aH_{a+1}$ and $S_s=T_aL_s\subseteq B$. By [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a), the $S_s$ are nested subobjects and $S_s/S_{s-1}\simeq T_a(L_s/L_{s-1})$, compatibly with the quotient maps. Also $S_0=0$: additivity gives $\mathrm{id}_{T_a0}=T_a(\mathrm{id}_0)=T_a(0)=0$, which makes $T_a0$ a zero object. The top subobject is $S_m=B$.

source.place: Final paragraph: splice finite filtrations by inverse images, starting at the last nonempty member of the closed chain. Exact transport uses Stacks Tag 010N, homology.tex, label lemma-exact-functor.

proof.text: For $0\le s\le m$ form $R_s=H\times_B S_s$, with maps $h_s:R_s\to H$, $p_s:R_s\to S_s$ and $j_s:S_s\hookrightarrow B$ satisfying $\pi h_s=j_sp_s$. These pullbacks exist directly from [def-sp-abelian]: take the kernel of $(\pi,-j_s):H\oplus S_s\to B$, whose maps from any object are exactly the compatible pairs. The map $h_s$ is monic: if $h_sx=h_sy$, then $j_sp_sx=\pi h_sx=\pi h_sy=j_sp_sy$; cancel $j_s$, then use uniqueness of the compatible pair. Each inclusion $S_{s-1}\hookrightarrow S_s$ gives an inclusion $i_s:R_{s-1}\hookrightarrow R_s$ by the same universal property. The pullback for $S_0=0$ is $\ker\pi$, so $R_0=u(K)$ as subobjects by the given kernel property of $u$. For $S_m=B$ the compatible pair $(\mathrm{id}_H,\pi)$ gives an inverse to $h_m$, hence $R_m=H$ as subobjects.

source.place: Final paragraph: splice finite filtrations by inverse images, starting at the last nonempty member of the closed chain. The kernel formula is Stacks homology.tex, Example label example-fibre-product-pushouts following Tag 010D; its universal property is checked here.

proof.text: Each $p_s:R_s\to S_s$ is epic. Indeed, for any $y:V\to S_s$, apply [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](a) to the epimorphism $\pi$ and $j_sy:V\to B$. It supplies an epimorphism $\rho:V\prime\to V$ and $x:V\prime\to H$ with $\pi x=j_sy\rho$. The compatible pair $(x,y\rho)$ defines $z:V\prime\to R_s$ with $p_sz=y\rho$. The converse direction of (a) now says that $p_s$ is epic. Here $\pi$ is epic because it is a cokernel: maps agreeing after $\pi$ are equal by uniqueness in its universal property. This argument also applies when $S_s=0$.

source.place: Final paragraph: splice finite filtrations by inverse images, starting at the last nonempty member of the closed chain. The refinement characterization proves the pullback-epimorphism assertion of Stacks Tag 05PK without assuming a splitting.

proof.text: Fix $1\le s\le m$ and let $f_s:S_{s-1}\hookrightarrow S_s$, $q_s:S_s\to D_s=S_s/S_{s-1}$ be its cokernel. The composite $e_s=q_sp_s:R_s\to D_s$ is epic, since $p_s$ is epic and every cokernel is epic. It kills $i_s$. To prove exactness, let $y:V\to R_s$ satisfy $e_sy=0$. By [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](c), there are an epimorphism $\rho:V\prime\to V$ and $x:V\prime\to S_{s-1}$ with $p_sy\rho=f_sx$. Thus $\pi h_sy\rho=j_sf_sx=j_{s-1}x$. The pair $(h_sy\rho,x)$ defines $z:V\prime\to R_{s-1}$. Its image $i_sz$ equals $y\rho$: their composites with the monomorphism $h_s$ are both $h_sy\rho$. Part (b) of the same node proves that $R_{s-1}\xrightarrow{i_s}R_s\xrightarrow{e_s}D_s$ is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](a), $e_s$ is a cokernel of $i_s$. Therefore $R_s/R_{s-1}\simeq D_s\simeq T_a(L_s/L_{s-1})$. The first isomorphism is the unique map intertwining the quotient projections; the reverse map is provided by the other cokernel universal property, and their composites are identities by uniqueness.

source.place: Final paragraph: splice finite filtrations by inverse images, starting at the last nonempty member of the closed chain. Quotient identification by exactness and epimorphic cokernels; compare Stacks Tags 08N3 and 08N4, homology.tex, labels lemma-cartesian-kernel and lemma-cartesian-cocartesian.

proof.text: For $0\le r\le n_a$ let $A_r\subseteq H$ be represented by $K_{a,r}\hookrightarrow K\xrightarrow{u}H$. Then $A_0=0$ and $A_{n_a}=u(K)=R_0$. For $1\le r\le n_a$, [lem-sfb-subobject-inclusion-cokernel], with $f$ and $g$ the two composite inclusions into $H$, $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ and $\phi:K_{a,r-1}\hookrightarrow K_{a,r}$, identifies $A_r/A_{r-1}$ with $Q_{a,r}$. All its hypotheses hold because the composites are monic and $f=g\phi$. Concatenate $A_0,\ldots,A_{n_a}$ and $R_1,\ldots,R_m$, omitting the repeated junction $R_0=A_{n_a}$. This has length $n_a+m=N_a$. Its first quotients are $Q_{a,r}=T_{a,a}Q_{a,r}$. By step 4 and the induction isomorphisms its remaining quotients are $T_aT_{a+1,c}Q_{c,s}\simeq T_{a,c}Q_{c,s}$, in precisely the original order. A functor sends an isomorphism to an isomorphism by applying it to the two inverse maps. This completes the descending induction and gives the prescribed images and inverse images.

source.place: Final paragraph: splice finite filtrations by inverse images, starting at the last nonempty member of the closed chain. Assemble the two lists after identifying their junction; the categorical representative comparison is the cited closed node.

proof.text: For the label assertion, iterating the assumed inclusions $T_b(P_{b+1,v})\subseteq P_{b,v}$ shows that $T_{a,c}Q_{c,s}\in P_{a,v_{c,s}}$: at $a=c$ this is the hypothesis on $Q_{c,s}$, and decreasing $a$ once applies exactly one assumed inclusion. Isomorphism invariance then applies to each quotient isomorphism constructed above. Its label is unchanged, so any real number bounding all input labels also bounds all output labels. The construction allows repeated subobjects throughout. If $t=0$ it is its base case. If all $n_a=0$, descending induction gives a chain of length zero from zero to $H_a$, so $H_a$ is zero and its filtration is empty. More generally either list at a junction may have length zero; the endpoint identifications used in step 5 still hold. No argument selected a section of $\pi_a$.

source.place: Final paragraph: splice finite filtrations by inverse images, starting at the last nonempty member of the closed chain. Label transport and degenerate lengths in the same finite induction.
